title_or_hook: Midrange vs three in the clutch: a win-probability study (NBA)
summary: A multi-panel win-probability-added study of shot value in the clutch (last 5 minutes of the 4th quarter / OT), regular season and playoffs, answering a question from @Hurtsknowsball (quoted in the post). Short answer as posted: usually the three stays better, but the midrange closes the gap when tied or ahead late, and beats the three when the clock forces a rushed shot. Browser-read figures (approx, small text): tied in the final 12 seconds, a midrange is worth about 139% of a three's WPA (regular season) and about 189% in the playoff version; tied and rushed inside 24 seconds, about 199%. Mechanism panels: three-point make rates fall in the clutch, and contested rates on threes nearly double (approx bars: about 17% contested earlier in games vs about 29% on rushed clutch threes). The general lesson transfers: an action's value is not a constant (the league-wide 'midrange is dead' prior) but a function of game state (score, time, pressure state), and in the states that decide games the ranking flips.
